required_delta_from_previous_checkpoint.canonical_en: New postoperative recovery evidence: incision is dry, drains are patent, and vital signs are stable; rehabilitation and VTE-risk monitoring continue.
The state has progressed from immediate completion of surgery to early postoperative inpatient management, with permanent pathology and subsequent treatment assessment still pending.

resolved_problems.canonical_en: Diagnostic sampling of the right breast primary tumor has been completed.
Definitive surgery of the right breast has been completed
CT pulmonary angiography showed no obvious pulmonary artery abnormality

treatment_readiness.canonical_en: Local definitive surgery has been completed; conditions are present to continue postoperative monitoring and rehabilitation management, but conditions are not yet present, based on current evidence, to complete final staging, adjuvant-treatment decision-making, or safely stop management.

hard_failure_rules_en: Do not equate negative axillary FNA or negative sentinel frozen sections with final lymph node negativity.
Do not equate no obvious abnormality on pulmonary artery CTA with absence of VTE
Do not determine safe cessation or discharge before postoperative assessment, drainage management, and continuity-of-care arrangements are completed
Do not infer complete TNM staging or an adjuvant treatment regimen when permanent pathology has not been disclosed.
critical_omission_rules_en: Right calf intermuscular vein thrombosis must be retained and managed.
Postoperative incision, drainage, and vital signs must continue to be monitored.
Permanent pathology must be followed up and subsequent oncology-treatment assessment completed.
Continuity follow-up and drainage management after discharge must be planned.
preliminary_risk_triggers_en: Current postoperative vital signs are stable.
Right calf intermuscular venous thrombosis is an active safety issue
Final pathology and staging have not been completed
The drainage tube remains in place; it is currently inappropriate to directly determine that discharge is possible or that it can be safely stopped.

stopping.rationale_en: The dry incision, patent drains, and stable vital signs support an early stable postoperative state. However, permanent pathology, final staging, VTE management, and continuity planning remain incomplete. Care should not be stopped, and unconditional follow-up is not yet safe; postoperative management should continue while awaiting the key pathology result.
remaining_blockers_en: Permanent pathology of the breast and lymph nodes and final staging have not been disclosed.
The drainage tube remains in place and postoperative recovery is still at an early stage.
The perioperative management plan for right calf intermuscular venous thrombosis needs to be clarified.
Adjuvant treatment and arrangements for continuous follow-up have not been completed.

question.question_en: At this time point, use only available evidence to identify key evidence, supported claims, patient state, appropriate next actions, and whether stopping or follow-up is safe.

completion_criteria_en: Right breast invasive carcinoma has been supported by biopsy pathology and confirmed by immunohistochemistry to be of breast origin.
partial_criteria_en: Highly suspicious on imaging and clinically, but without pathological confirmation yet
safety_invalidation_rules_en: If subsequent pathology negates invasive breast carcinoma, the diagnosis needs to be re-examined.

completion_criteria_en: Obtain complete permanent pathology and complete final staging and adjuvant-treatment assessment.
Complete the perioperative VTE risk and existing thrombosis management plan
partial_criteria_en: Preoperative VTE and pulmonary artery assessment and sentinel frozen sections have been completed.
Definitive surgery has been completed, but permanent pathology and final staging are incomplete.
safety_invalidation_rules_en: Do not substitute negative FNA or frozen section for permanent-pathology staging
If thrombus progression, bleeding, or postoperative instability occurs, treatment readiness becomes invalid.

completion_criteria_en: Right simple mastectomy and planned sentinel lymph-node and related axillary management have been completed.
partial_criteria_en: Surgery has been completed, but postoperative recovery management and pathology review are still needed.
safety_invalidation_rules_en: If major postoperative complications occur or additional local treatment is needed, the clinical pathway cannot be regarded as fully completed

completion_criteria_en: Postoperative activity recovery and VTE management plan are clear.
Complete necessary pathology review and linkage to subsequent treatment.
partial_criteria_en: The current incision is dry, drainage is unobstructed, vital signs are stable, and rehabilitation and VTE monitoring have begun.
safety_invalidation_rules_en: Do not determine completion if there is wound infection, bleeding, drainage abnormality, thrombus progression, or vital-sign instability

completion_criteria_en: Meet clear discharge criteria and complete drain, wound, VTE, and rehabilitation guidance.
Arrange permanent pathology review, oncology specialist assessment, and subsequent follow-up
partial_criteria_en: Postoperative recovery and rehabilitation management are in place, but the patient remains hospitalized and the drainage tube is in place; there is no evidence that arrangements for continuity of care have been completed.
safety_invalidation_rules_en: Must not determine completion when VTE management, drainage management, or pathology follow-up is not clearly defined
Do not discharge or transition to routine follow-up when unstable postoperative problems are present
